guard: the discovery document a real auth-service serves over the wire is accepted by the real consumer `cotal meshes add --from` validates it with, and names the same provider the registered AuthProvider answers to
why: THE DEFECT THIS GUARDS was invisible to two panels because each side's tests build the shape
that side expects: the producer's smoke asserted the flat fields it had just written, and the
consumer's smoke fed itself a hand-written `userAuth` fixture. Nothing fed the server's actual
bytes to the consumer. So the mutations worth running here are the ones that put the producer
back the way it was and ask whether the seam notices. A guard that cannot detect the original
bug is decoration.
M1 IS THE ONE THIS BRANCH ADDS, and it is a different kind of defect from the other two. The
shape half is already fixed on main; what was still held only by agreement is the provider
NAME, which appeared as a bare "cotal" literal at three sites. Two of them are the two ends of
one contract: the name the registered provider answers to, and the name the served document
advertises. They are now one exported constant, and M1 re-hardcodes a divergent literal at the
bundle end. That mutation is INVISIBLE to the consumer -- checkUserBundle requires a provider
name, not any particular one -- so it can only be caught by a cell that compares the served
name against `cotalAuthProvider.name` rather than against a string the test also chose. The
suite grades the OUTCOME (the two names agree) rather than the mechanism (both read one
constant), because grading the mechanism would pass a tree where both sites moved together.
AFTER-RESTORE REBUILD, and it is not tidiness. The suite starts the auth-service by
self-re-exec, and that child imports `@cotal-ai/auth` -- i.e. dist, not the source the mutation
edits. Hence the build in `command`. mutation-proof restores SOURCE and not artifacts, so
without `afterRestore` a graded run would leave a local dist compiled FROM THE MUTANT: a
daemon serving the wrong document with the source looking correct. dist is gitignored, so git
cannot be the recovery for it. Each mutation rebuilds after its own restore.
M2 FIRST CAME BACK INCONCLUSIVE, AND THE FAULT WAS THE SUITE'S, so it was fixed on the test
side rather than by re-aiming the mutation. Section C stripped `userAuth.provider` from the
served document with a bare `delete (doc.userAuth as ...).provider`. Under M2 there IS no
wrapper -- which is the whole point of M2 -- so that line threw a TypeError, the run died before
printing its completion line, and the tool refused to count an unfinished run as a kill. It was
right to refuse: a suite that crashes instead of reporting cannot say how much it checked, and
red-because-it-died is not red-because-it-noticed. The strip is now narrowed before the delete,
so the suite survives the exact failure it grades and the kill lands on the seam cell.

mutations.name: M1 the bundle re-hardcodes a provider name, diverging from the one the registry dispatches to
mutations.expectRed: the served provider name IS the registered provider's own name (no drift between them)
mutations.cell: the served provider name IS the registered provider's own name (no drift between them)
mutations.note: The exact regression the constant exists to prevent, and the one the CONSUMER cannot see: checkUserBundle demands a provider name, not a correct one, so this document parses cleanly and registers an entry that resolves to nothing. Only the cross-check against `cotalAuthProvider.name` can catch it.

mutations.name: M2 the served document loses its userAuth wrapper entirely (the original shape defect)
mutations.expectRed: the LIVE served document is accepted by checkUserBundle (the `meshes add --from` consumer)
mutations.cell: the LIVE served document is accepted by checkUserBundle (the `meshes add --from` consumer)
mutations.note: The original defect, reintroduced at the point the document is finalized. The bundle is written in two phases (composed before listen(), pinned after, because endpoints.url is only known post-bind) and both act on the same closure-shared object, so deleting the key here removes the wrapper the composer created -- the served document goes flat without touching composeUserBundle.

mutations.name: M3 the post-bind pin is skipped, leaving the wrapper present but pinning the empty string
mutations.expectRed: the LIVE served document is accepted by checkUserBundle (the `meshes add --from` consumer)
mutations.cell: the LIVE served document is accepted by checkUserBundle (the `meshes add --from` consumer)
mutations.note: The two-phase trap: the wrapper survives but keeps its pre-bind empty URL, so the document advertises an exchange endpoint nothing listens on. The kill lands on the SEAM cell rather than the pinned-URL cell, because checkUserBundle refuses first -- assertUserAuthInfo drops an empty endpoints.url (mesh-registry.ts spreads the url only when truthy) and meshes-add.ts then refuses with `pins no exchange endpoint`. Distinct from M2 in what it breaks (a present-but-hollow wrapper vs an absent one) even though both surface at the same assertion, and worth keeping because the shipped validator -- not a bespoke check -- is what closes it.
